about.title: Oman's first LPG bottler
body: National Gas Company is a fully Omani-owned public joint stock company, listed on the Muscat Stock Exchange. It was incorporated in 1979 to meet the growing need for LPG, and in 1981 it started bottling, the beginning of the LPG industry in Oman.

From bottling plants across the Sultanate, the company grew into bulk supply, gas engineering, SNG, cutting gas, aerosol propellant and lubricants, and into LPG markets abroad, today chiefly Malaysia and Saudi Arabia.
more: In the late 1970s, local dealers had to travel to Dubai and Abu Dhabi to collect cylinders, and shortages were common because Omani dealers were served last. The first chairman, Mr. Mohd Abdul Rasool Al Jamali, was instrumental in setting up a bottling plant at home.

A fleet of tankers lifts bulk LPG from refineries in the Sultanate to the plants, where it is bottled into cylinders in safe, controlled conditions. A separate projects and design department handles engineering, procurement, installation, commissioning, testing and after-sales service.
The company's logo was renewed at its 25th anniversary in 2006: the dark blue flame stands for pure energy and continuous innovation, the light blue flame for a caring hand.

items.title: LPG installation
items.text: Bulk LPG systems from 3,000 to 300,000 litres, designed, fabricated and commissioned by our engineers.

detail.intro: National Gas has installed some of the largest LPG systems in Oman and the GCC, from 3,000 to 300,000 litres.
body: The team takes projects from design and fabrication to commissioning, and then keeps them supplied: bulk storage at strategic points across the Sultanate and the largest fleet of bulk tankers and bobtails in Oman.

We have designed, installed and commissioned LPG systems for poultry, glass, ceramic and powder plants across the GCC, and our engineers advise customers on running installations at international standards of safety and efficiency.
points: Clean burn, no carbon deposits
No spillage, no fumes
No pilferage from a closed, pressurised system
Higher efficiency than diesel

items.title: Synthetic Natural Gas
items.text: LPG blended with air to replace natural gas: base load, standby or peak shaving, 20 to 2,000 MMBTU/hr.

detail.intro: SNG is LPG blended with a diluent, usually compressed air, at the ratio that matches the Wobbe Index of natural gas. Burners see the same fuel.
body: National Gas designs, supplies, installs and commissions SNG systems with the LPG storage and bulk supply behind them, working with leading SNG equipment makers. Systems range from 20 to 2,000 MMBTU/hr for steel rolling mills, DRI and pelletising plants, ceramics, construction materials, aluminium, float glass and fibre glass.

The company built the first SNG system in Oman in 2008, the first in the GCC, and in 2011 the largest SNG system for a major international steel plant in Saudi Arabia. A 24x7 service team handles installation, testing and troubleshooting.
points: Base load, where natural gas is not available
Standby, when the natural gas supply is cut or under maintenance
Peak shaving, to cover shortages and price peaks

items.title: Gas engineering
items.text: Turnkey bottling plants, pressure reducing and metering stations, township gas and natural gas pipelines.

detail.intro: National Gas takes on turnkey design, engineering and commissioning of LPG bottling plants, de-odorising units, aerosol filling systems, autogas refuelling stations, pressure reducing and metering stations, SNG systems, gas-powered power systems and gas refrigeration.
body: Customers have used our gas engineering for bulk LPG and SNG installations, piped gas distribution, natural gas pressure reducing stations, LPG-based mobile heat treatment and LPG-based enhanced oil recovery.
We integrate small to large industrial installations and township piped gas networks for LPG and natural gas. In 2009 National Gas set up the first integrated township gas system in Sohar.
points: LPG bottling plants
Pressure reducing and metering stations
Township piped gas networks
Natural gas pipelines
Gas-powered power and refrigeration

items.title: Diesel to LPG conversion
items.text: Feasibility, dual-fuel burners and a bulk tank: commissioned within 3 to 4 months of the order.

detail.intro: National Gas converts industries from diesel, natural gas and other fuels to LPG, and has converted many plants already.
body: One litre of diesel is roughly equal to 0.796 kg of LPG, so about 20% less LPG is used for the same energy. To produce 2,000 MMBtu takes roughly 56,000 litres of diesel or 44,000 kg of LPG.
After conversion both fuels can still be used separately. The bulk tank and installation become an asset, and their payback is usually within two years.
points: Fill in the fuel plan with current fuel details
Check whether the burner is dual-fuel
Feasibility study, commercial and technical
Proposal and a 3 to 5 year LPG supply agreement
Commissioning within 3 to 4 months of the PO

items.title: Enhanced oil recovery
items.text: LPG-fired steam for oilfields: National Gas publishes a 3 to 6 month payback and at least 40% fuel savings.

detail.intro: Enhanced oil recovery, or tertiary recovery, extracts crude that cannot be produced any other way. National Gas supplies LPG-fuelled systems for it and explored the segment in 2014.
body: Steam injection and steam flooding heat the reservoir: the oil's viscosity drops, it expands and flows more easily. National Gas supplies the LPG side: storage, vaporisers and burners selected for the customer's steam generator.
Equipment is chosen per site: mobile or fixed vaporisers, wheel-mounted or fixed tanks, burners sized to the flow rate.
points: Fuel requirement for the OTSG (flow rate and input pressure)
Batch or continuous process
Back-up or buffer stock required

National Gas is authorised by Civil Defence to test LPG tanks for bulk installations, and supplies LPG fire-fighting, deluge and peak-shaving systems.

items.title: Safety and consumer awareness
items.text: Safety tips with every cylinder, road shows with the ROP and Civil Defence, and the Safety Pays school campaign.

detail.intro: In the LPG business safety comes first: for employees, contractors, customers and the public.
body: National Gas works on the two points bottlers do not control directly: homes and the distribution network. Safety tips go out with every cylinder, leaflets and road shows run in the capital and the interior with the Royal Oman Police and Civil Defence, and the Safety Pays campaign reaches children through school contests.

With Civil Defence, National Gas is developing safety training for distributors on cylinder handling, installation and emergency action. The QHSE policy sets the aim plainly: no injuries, occupational illnesses, unsafe practices or pollution.
points: Open all doors and windows fully
Do not switch any lights, fans or appliances on or off
Close the cylinder valve and switch off the regulator
Put out any cigarette or flame
Check for leaks with soapy water, never with a flame

items.title: LPG cylinders
items.text: 22 kg cylinders for homes and 44 kg cylinders for restaurants, camps and canteens, filled at our own bottling plants.
body: National Gas supplies LP Gas in cylinders from its bottling plants through a widespread network of distributors that covers almost every area of North Oman. Cylinders come mainly in 22 kg and 44 kg sizes, and to a lesser extent in 11 kg and as barbecue cylinders.
The 22 kg cylinder is easy to carry and store, and most households use it for cooking and water heating. Restaurants, labour camps and canteens use the 44 kg cylinder for cooking and heating.

Cylinders are designed, made and tested to the Omani standard OS-120:1986 or equivalent, and are tested again at intervals so that only safe cylinders reach homes and businesses. Every cylinder filled at National Gas carries the company's Silver Seal: the right quantity of gas, in a safe cylinder.

items.title: D-Cylinder
items.text: A fixed 440-litre cylinder for hotels, restaurants and factories, filled on site by bobtail and billed by the meter.
body: National Gas designed and introduced the D-Cylinder, built to DOT-4BW-250 / ASME Section VIII Division I. It stays fixed in the customer's gas bank; a National Gas bobtail fills it on site, and the bobtail's flow meter records exactly how much LPG went in. That is the amount invoiced.

A level gauge shows what is left, so customers pay for what they use and no gas is wasted. Handling cylinders by hand and leaks from hoses go away, and there is no need for the unsafe habit of putting cylinders in hot water.
More than 100 customers in Muscat, Sohar, Nizwa and Izki use D-Cylinders, from Lulu to Muscat Bakery.

items.title: Bulk LPG
items.text: Bulk LPG for factories, hotels and resorts, delivered by the largest fleet of tankers and bobtails in Oman.
body: Bulk LPG gives industrial users the flexibility to run several applications safely from one supply. Small and medium industries use it in food, ceramics, glass, metal works and dairies, and hotels and resorts use it for boilers, ovens and kitchens.
LP Gas is the preferred fuel where a clean burn matters: boilers, ovens and furnaces in hospitality, food and dairy, and direct firing in glass and ceramics.

National Gas runs the largest fleet of bulk tankers and bobtails in Oman, with bulk storage at strategic points across the Sultanate. Internal procedures and scheduling are designed so that customers never run out of gas, and our engineers advise on running bulk installations safely and efficiently.

items.title: NC+ cutting gas
items.text: A hydrocarbon cutting gas with an additive, used instead of acetylene for cutting, brazing and heat treatment.
body: National Gas developed NC+, a hydrocarbon industrial gas mixed with an additive that raises flame temperature and leaves a fine cut finish. It replaces the oxy-acetylene mixture traditionally used to cut steel.

NC+ is non-toxic, stable in liquid and gas form, has a low backfire tendency and cannot auto-ignite. A pungent smell makes leaks easy to detect. One fuel covers hand cutting, machine cutting, flame hardening, metalising, brazing, soldering, pre-heating and stress relieving.
National Gas started the NC+ business in Oman in 2008 and took it to the UAE and other countries from 2010. NC+ is present in Oman, the UAE, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Malaysia.

items.title: Commercial propane
items.text: Commercial and industrial grade propane for post-weld heat treatment and stress relief, in 44 kg cylinders or in bulk.
body: National Gas supplies commercial and industrial grade propane for post-weld heat treatment, stress relief and other jobs that need a high heat value.
Propane comes in 44 kg cylinders. For larger needs, it is delivered in bulk by semi-trailers fitted with safety equipment and vaporisers.
Grades range from 60% and 70% up to 90% propane, and other ratios can be matched on request.

items.title: Aerosol propellant
items.text: De-odorised LPG propellant from our Rusayl and Madha plants, a CFC-free choice for sprays and food-grade packs.
body: National Gas runs de-odorising plants at its Rusayl and Madha facilities, where it produces aerosol propellant: an environmentally friendlier alternative to ozone-depleting CFC propellants. Production started in 2005.
To keep the product clean, the plant uses a fully separate system of dedicated pipelines, pumps and a storage tank, and dedicated bobtails deliver only aerosol propellant.
Typical uses include pesticides, air fresheners, perfumes, cosmetics, spray paint and food-grade packaging.

items.title: HP Lubricants
items.text: Automotive, industrial and speciality oils and greases from HPCL, marketed in Oman by National Gas.
body: National Gas offers HP Lubricants, 'Power to Perform', from HPCL, one of the world's largest lube marketers. HPCL owns one of the largest lube base-oil refineries and makes more than 450 grades of lubricants, greases and specialities.
The range covers transport, railways, manufacturing, mining, shipping, agriculture and power. National Gas launched its lubricants division in 2016 and HP Lubricants in Oman in September 2020.

items.title: PSA nitrogen and oxygen generators
items.text: On-site nitrogen or oxygen from compressed air, at high purity, sized to your plant.
body: Pressure swing adsorption makes nitrogen or oxygen from compressed air on site, so you produce gas where and when you need it, at the purity you need. Air is the only raw material.
National Gas designs generators to the customer's specification, including higher capacities and extreme ambient conditions.

highlights.title: Cheaper than liquid nitrogen
highlights.text: No orders, deliveries or high-pressure cylinders to store.

highlights.title: Control of purity
highlights.text: Better control of gas purity, and of product quality downstream.

highlights.title: Modular
highlights.text: Upgrade later by adding banks to the existing system.

items.title: Membrane nitrogen generators
items.text: Hollow-fibre membrane units that make nitrogen from compressed air, efficient at lower purities.
body: Hollow-fibre membranes separate nitrogen from compressed air for on-site production. They are most efficient at lower product purities.
Units run automatically and unattended at low operating pressure, with no hazardous storage, and are compact enough to transport and install easily.

items.title: LPG and natural gas equipment
items.text: Vaporisers, pressure reducing stations, metering, gas detection, fire-fighting systems and valves.
body: National Gas supplies complete LPG systems and individual equipment: vaporisers, pumps, regulators, pressure reducing stations, metering systems, secondary pipeline work, gas detectors, LPG leak detection, fire-fighting, deluge and peak-shaving systems, and all kinds of LPG valves.
For natural gas, the team handles pipeline work and the installation and commissioning of NG pressure reducing and metering stations.

news.title: NGC calls for LPG price review amid rising costs
news.summary: National Gas has asked the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion again to revise the regulated OMR 1.9 rate for a 22 kg cylinder, unchanged since 1994.
body: National Gas Company SAOG resubmitted its request for a revision of the regulated LPG cylinder price to the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion in early July 2026, CEO Dr Rachid Majjad told shareholders on the first-half earnings call.

The regulated rate of OMR 1.9 for the standard 22 kg cylinder applies to the bottler's part of the supply chain and is distinct from the retail price. According to Dr Majjad, the company's LPG purchase price has risen by around 50%, alongside payroll, transport and tax costs.

As an interim step, National Gas has been withdrawing discounts to traders and distributors: in selected areas from January 2026 and in Muscat from 1 September. The company is also awaiting guidance on colour-coded cylinders for each bottler; it plans yellow cylinders under its MiraGas brand, already used in Malaysia, with self-closing valves.

news.title: First-half 2026: revenue up, back in profit
news.summary: Group revenue rose to RO 47.6 million and the group made an after-tax profit of RO 298,072, against a loss a year earlier.
body: National Gas reported group revenue of RO 47,585,350 for the six months to 30 June 2026, against RO 43,741,406 in the first half of 2025.

Group profit after tax was RO 298,072, compared with a loss of RO 348,026. The Chairman's report credits the transformation plan launched in 2023 and a profitable Malaysian LPG business; project delays affected the Saudi unit.

news.title: National Gas Saudi unit and Zamil win LPG licences
news.summary: NGC Energy Saudi LLC and Zamil Group won licences for cylinder filling and storage in Jeddah and Jazan and for wholesale LPG distribution across Saudi Arabia.
body: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy named a consortium of NGC Energy Saudi LLC, wholly owned by National Gas, and Zamil Group Holding Company among the winners of eight LPG filling, storage and bulk distribution licences.

The licences cover LPG cylinder filling and storage facilities in Jeddah and Jazan and wholesale LPG distribution across the Kingdom. Developing the two plants, including land and approvals, is expected to take about 24 months; wholesale distribution should begin within about 12 months.
National Gas has signed a memorandum of understanding with Zamil Group Investment Company and expects definitive agreements once regulatory approvals are in place.

news.title: Annual General Meeting held online
news.summary: Shareholders met online to approve the 2025 reports, elect a new Board and appoint auditors.
body: The 2026 Annual General Meeting of National Gas Company SAOG took place online through mcd.om on 25 March 2026, with a second call on 29 March.
The agenda included the 2025 reports, the election of a new Board of Directors, up to RO 10,000 for community support and the appointment of auditors.

news.title: National Gas acquires 80% stake in Samahram Gas
news.summary: The purchase of 80% of Samahram Gas, an LPG filling and distribution company in Dhofar, was completed on 4 June 2025.
body: National Gas told the Muscat Stock Exchange that it had completed the acquisition of an 80% stake in Samahram Gas Company on 4 June 2025, after regulatory approvals.

Samahram Gas fills LPG cylinders, installs and operates central gas systems and supplies bulk LPG in the Dhofar Governorate. National Gas said the deal strengthens its footprint in Oman's LPG market and should add to group revenue and net income.

news.title: HP Lubricants aims for a bigger share of Oman's lubricant market
news.summary: HP Lubricants, sold in Oman by National Gas, plans to grow its sales; National Gas entered lubricants in 2016.
body: HP Lubricants, marketed in Oman by National Gas, set out plans to capture a larger share of the Omani lubricant segment.
National Gas CEO Dr Rachid Majjad noted that the company entered the lubricants business in 2016.

news.title: National Gas sells its India investment for $15.6mn
news.summary: The 60% stake in NGC Energy India, which was building an LPG terminal at Krishnapatnam, was sold for US$15.61 million.
body: National Gas completed the sale of its 60% stake in NGC Energy India Pvt Ltd to Petregaz India Holdings for US$15.61 million, including a US$3.5 million premium. The proceeds were earmarked to reduce debt.
The same report noted the company's August 2022 decision to exit its UAE operations.

news.title: National Gas sells its 51% stake in Unigaz
news.summary: Unigaz LLC, a gas distribution and cooking-gas pipe maintenance company, bought back National Gas's 51% for RO 407,000.
body: National Gas sold its entire 51% stake in the Unigaz LLC joint venture, which distributes gas and maintains cooking gas pipes in Oman, for RO 407,000.

news.title: National Gas partners with HP Lubricants in Oman
news.summary: HP Lubricants was launched in Oman on 6 September 2020 through National Gas, which HPCL later named a best performer.
body: National Gas launched HP Lubricants in Oman on 6 September 2020, offering HPCL's global portfolio of automotive, industrial and speciality lubricants.
HPCL recognised National Gas with a best performer award.

news.title: Consumer safety is the most important, says National Gas
news.summary: A national LPG safety campaign used videos, social media and print to teach safe cylinder handling.
body: National Gas ran an LPG safety awareness campaign through videos, social media and print, reminding households how to handle cylinders and what to do if they smell gas.
The article described National Gas as running six strategically located plants and more than 40 years of service.

news.title: National Gas joint venture to build an LPG terminal in India
news.summary: NGC Energy India (60%) and Petredec (40%) planned a 30,000-tonne LPG import terminal at Krishnapatnam port.
body: NGC Energy India, a joint venture of National Gas (60%) and Petredec (40%), announced a refrigerated LPG import terminal at Krishnapatnam port with 30,000 tonnes of storage and 1.4 million tonnes a year of throughput.
National Gas later sold its stake, in September 2022.

faq.a: LPG stands for liquefied petroleum gas. It is a mixture of propane and butane, compressed and stored as a liquid for use as fuel.
LPG is a by-product of oil and natural gas production, and is also extracted at refineries and gas processing plants.

faq.q: How do I buy LPG from National Gas?
faq.a: National Gas supplies LPG cylinders through its distributor network, and delivers bulk LPG and D-Cylinder refills directly to commercial and industrial customers. Call +968 2416 2646 or write to sales@nationalgasco.net.
Online, at company outlets, or by bank transfer.

faq.q: What should I do if I smell gas?
faq.a: Open all doors and windows fully. Do not switch lights, fans or any appliance on or off. Close the cylinder valve and switch off the regulator, and put out any flame or cigarette.

faq.q: How do I check a cylinder for leaks?
faq.a: Use a sponge or brush with soapy water on the joints. Never use a match or a flame. If there is a leak, close the valve and do not use the cylinder until an expert has repaired it.

faq.q: Why is LPG heavier than air a safety point?
faq.a: LPG vapour is 1.5 to 2 times heavier than air, so a leak collects at ground level. Keep cylinders upright, out of the sun and outside the kitchen, never in a pit or basement.
